topics.topic: Classification and handling of photo_date representations, including Z, malformed values, and alternate timezone spellings
questions: Does a `photo_date` ending in `Z` count as a date without an offset that passes, or as the old date that normative rule 1 says must stop delivery?
Exactly which representations count as dates without an offset, especially whether a value ending in Z belongs to that class and whether malformed or non-ISO date strings pass?
What must the flow do with a non-date, a malformed date, or a date using another timezone spelling?

quotes: A `photo_date` ending in `Z` or in an offset `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM` is an old date.

When the list holds an old date, or cannot be read, the flow places and publishes nothing for that
   project and tells the owner which project needs the repair.
INV-17: a project holding a date with an offset is detected before delivery, and a project holding only dates without an offset passes. The calling flow's own stop is shown when that flow exists.
judgement.divergence: A `Z` suffix is expressly old, but for a readable malformed value or an alternate timezone spelling one implementation treats only the listed suffixes as old and continues, while another refuses unsupported date representations; the owner and calling flow observe delivery versus a repair stop.
judgement.why: The rule resolves `Z` as old but does not decide whether readable malformed values or unlisted timezone spellings are non-old values that pass or invalid values that stop delivery.

witness.initial: A project's readable staff photo list contains `photo_date` value `not-a-date`.
events: The calling flow reads the project's staff photo list before placing anything.
The calling flow classifies the value and decides whether to continue.
outcomes: The flow finds none of the listed old-date suffixes and continues toward delivery.
The flow treats the malformed value as unsupported, places and publishes nothing, and tells the owner that the project needs repair.
witness.observer: The owner and the calling flow
basis:
Before placing anything for a project, the calling flow reads that project's staff photo list in
   the Portal.

When the list holds an old date, or cannot be read, the flow places and publishes nothing for that
   project and tells the owner which project needs the repair.

topics.topic: Meaning and required observable outcome of a passing no-offset date case
questions: Which representations qualify as dates without an offset, and does “passes” mean only that the old-date gate accepts them or that the calling flow must proceed with delivery?
What observable result must the passing case demonstrate: only that the old-date gate permits continuation, or that placement and publication complete successfully?
Does “passes” mean only that the A11 date check permits the flow to continue, or that the test must show a completed delivery?

quotes: INV-17: a project holding a date with an offset is detected before delivery, and a project holding only dates without an offset passes. The calling flow's own stop is shown when that flow exists.

Before placing anything for a project, the calling flow reads that project's staff photo list in
   the Portal. A `photo_date` ending in `Z` or in an offset `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM` is an old date.

A delivery starts from an action of the owner in the workplace. The workplace lists the photos
that are ready, the owner chooses what to deliver, and the calling flow places, publishes and
marks each chosen photo in that order. The owner sees the result of each photo: delivered, or
failed with its reason. A failed photo does not stop the others. The service delivers nothing by
itself.
judgement.divergence: One implementation accepts every readable value lacking the listed suffixes and treats reaching the next check as a passing A11 case; another accepts only a valid timezone-naive datetime and requires completed placement and publication, so the owner and verification of the calling flow observe different acceptance and delivery results.
judgement.why: Neither the qualifying syntax of a no-offset date nor whether “passes” means passing this gate or completing delivery is specified.

outcomes: The date-only value passes the A11 gate, and the A11 passing case is satisfied even though the later step fails.

questions: What must the witness assert to demonstrate INV-17: detection alone, prevention of publication, prevention of both placement and publication, or the calling flow's reported repair message?
Which prohibited effects must the witness assert are absent when an old date is detected: publication only, both placement and publication, or every operation considered part of delivery?

INV-17: a project holding a date with an offset is detected before delivery, and a project holding only dates without an offset passes. The calling flow's own stop is shown when that flow exists.
judgement.divergence: A detector-only witness can pass while an implementation places a photo but does not publish it, whereas a witness asserting the normative stop fails unless both placement and publication are absent and the owner is told; the project state, owner, and verification suite observe the difference.

topics.topic: INV-17 evidence required before a calling flow exists and when flow-specific evidence becomes mandatory
questions: If no calling flow exists when the witness is assembled, must a later test show its stop once it exists, must the invariant witness fail as incomplete, or is detector-only evidence permanently sufficient?
If no concrete calling flow exists when the witness is implemented, what must the witness show for INV-17, and what later event makes the flow-specific stop evidence mandatory?

quotes: INV-17: a project holding a date with an offset is detected before delivery, and a project holding only dates without an offset passes. The calling flow's own stop is shown when that flow exists.
judgement.why: Before a calling flow exists the item requires detection and the passing case, and existence of the calling flow is the stated event that makes evidence of that flow's own stop mandatory.

topics.topic: Kernel service credential, validation method, and ownership state
questions: What credential does the kernel use, how is it presented and validated, and which later state owns that decision?

quotes: | Calling flow → deliverer | project id, file name, source id, Portal photo id | authenticated by the deliverer's own bearer token |

Every operation except the health answer requires exactly one `Authorization` field. Its value is
   the scheme `Bearer`, compared without regard to case as HTTP defines an authentication scheme, one
   space and the token, compared whole, case-sensitively and in constant time. A request without that
   field, with more than one, or with any other value is refused with the UNAUTHORIZED member of
   = models.RefusalCode before its identifiers or body are examined.

The token is generated with 256 bits from a cryptographic random source and is kept in a
   file in the encoding of the imported `TOKEN_ENCODING` constant: the 32 random bytes in URL-safe Base64, 43 characters of `A`-`Z`, `a`-`z`, `0`-`9`, `-` and `_`.
   The path is the `credential_file` run setting (A8). At the start it is read once; its last component must not be a
   link, while the folders above it belong to the installation and are taken as they stand, and the
   permissions judged are those of the file that is read. The file is decoded in that encoding, a byte sequence it cannot
   decode ending the start, and the characters of the imported `TOKEN_TRIM_CHARACTERS` constant (the ASCII
   space, tab, line feed, carriage return, vertical tab and form feed) are removed at both ends; no other
   character is removed. The service does not start when
   the path is a symbolic link or not a regular file, when the group or others have any permission on
   the file, or when what remains has fewer characters than the imported `TOKEN_MIN_LENGTH` constant or any character outside
   the imported `TOKEN_ALPHABET` constant, since a token with such a character could not be presented in
   the `Authorization` header.

The service listens on the loopback interface, the address of the imported `BIND_HOST` constant. A reverse proxy on the same host terminates
   HTTPS for any caller from outside. The service reads no forwarded header.
There is one principal: the calling flow of the owner. It may act on every confirmed connection.
judgement.why: A5 already selects the deliverer's bearer token, its presentation and comparison, its file validation and refusal behavior, and the single calling-flow principal; only deployment of the host and HTTPS route remains later.
